```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import time

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from torch import nn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

_ = torch.manual_seed(481)
digits = pd.read_csv("data/optdigits-test.csv", header=None)
x = torch.tensor(digits.iloc[:, :64].to_numpy(), dtype=torch.float32) / 16
y = torch.tensor(digits[64].to_numpy())
n_train = 1200
order = torch.randperm(len(x))
x_train, y_train = x[order[:n_train]], y[order[:n_train]]

_ = torch.manual_seed(1)
mlp = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(64, 32), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(32, 10))
loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
print(mlp)
```

The exercises use the same digits, split and network as the [feedforward networks chapter](feedforward-networks.qmd#exm-feedforward-network):
the `r format(nrow(py$digits), big.mark = ",")` images of [`data/optdigits-test.csv`](data/optdigits-test.csv) [@alpaydin1998optdigits],
with pixels divided by 16,
a random `r format(py$n_train, big.mark = ",")` of them as the [training set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set),
and an untrained [MLP](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-feedforward-network) with one [hidden layer](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-hidden-layer) of `r py$mlp[0]$out_features` [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu) [units](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit).
